reasons.C: Closest in movement and stance: long, winding sentences with interpolated asides ('so to say', 'it may be') set against short dry turns, quoted ad-words used ironically, and the same playful, mock-earnest confiding tone as the passage.
reasons.A: Catches the quoted-word irony and the chatty first person, but its run of short, parallel 'Every room is...' and 'There are old...' sentences is plainer and more repetitive than the passage's digressive, clause-heavy rhythm.
reasons.B: Smooth, even, modern-essay sentences with no quoted phrases, dashes or digressive asides; its measured, moralising stance and neat closing maxim lack the passage's whimsy and quirk.
